belief: Single people are less complete in God’s eyes.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that single people are less complete in God’s eyes, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Church activities built mostly around couples and families. Questions like “When are you getting married?” Feeling left out or invisible. Teaching that marriage is the goal of every Christian life. Loneliness or grief over not having a spouse.
teaches: Marriage is a good gift, and so is singleness. Jesus was single. Paul was single and called singleness a gift that frees a person for undivided devotion to the Lord. God promised the eunuch, who could have no family line, a name better than sons and daughters. In Christ, every believer is made complete. Your worth and wholeness come from God, not from your marital status, and God places the lonely in families, including the family of the church.
self_statements: My life won’t really start until I’m married.
Something must be wrong with me.
Single people don’t fit in the church.
errors: Measuring your life against married friends.
Treating marriage as the only path to a complete life.
Overlooking Scripture’s honor for single people.
questions: Was Jesus less complete because He was single?
What does Colossians 2:10 say about being complete?
What did God promise the eunuch in Isaiah 56?
Where does my worth come from?
How could I use this season for God and others?
Who are my “family” in the church?
truth: Single people are not less complete in God’s eyes. I am made complete in Christ. Jesus was single, and Paul called singleness a gift. My worth comes from God, not my marital status. I can honor my desires and also use this season fully, and God places me in His family.

prayer: Father, thank You that I am complete in Christ. Help me reject the lie that single people are less complete in Your eyes. Meet my desires and my loneliness, place me in a loving family of believers, and help me live this season fully for You. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
